description: Source-checked public opportunity statements; NOT proof of approval, individual eligibility, settled revenue, or current service availability.

opportunities.title: Twilio A2P 10DLC registration has fixed and recurring costs before message usage
opportunities.claim: Twilio's published U.S. A2P 10DLC fee schedule lists a $4.50 one-time Brand registration fee for Sole Proprietor and Low Volume Standard brands, a $15 one-time Campaign vetting fee, and recurring campaign fees that include $2/month for Sole Proprietor Starter and $1.50/month for Low Volume Mixed use cases. Standard Brand registration is listed at $46, with campaign fees varying by use case. Carrier pass-through fees are additional to Twilio's base messaging rates.
opportunities.why_now: First source-checked telecom cost baseline added to the SECONDS MATTER ledger. It makes visible the minimum fixed and recurring customer-specific costs that earlier readiness notes described only generally; this is a newly recorded baseline, not a newly announced fee change.
opportunities.value: No cash or credits. A Sole Proprietor path has at least $19.50 in one-time Brand plus Campaign vetting fees and $2/month recurring campaign fees before phone-number, base SMS, and carrier costs; actual path depends on business/tax-ID status and use case.
opportunities.eligibility: U.S. senders using 10-digit long-code numbers for application-to-person messaging. Sole Proprietor registration is for eligible individuals/businesses without an EIN; businesses with an EIN generally require Low Volume Standard or Standard registration according to traffic and use case.
opportunities.friction: Requires brand and campaign details, use-case vetting, opt-in/opt-out and HELP handling, recurring campaign fees, per-message Twilio charges, and carrier pass-through fees. Customer account ownership, tax-ID category, consent, and registration status are not verified.
opportunities.observed_delta: Adds exact one-time and recurring A2P fee components to the journal; prior notes mentioned registration friction but did not preserve this cost floor.
opportunities.anti_leverage: Do not absorb client registration, number, or message costs. Prefer customer-owned telecom accounts or explicit pass-through pricing; otherwise small per-customer fees can erase service margin.

opportunities.title: Invoca 2026 home-services benchmark shows substantial unanswered-call gap
opportunities.claim: Invoca's July 2026 home-services benchmark says 52% of all inbound calls in its platform's home-services dataset were answered by a person; the answer rate rises to 65% for calls longer than 15 seconds and 73% for calls longer than 30 seconds. The report says its analysis uses anonymized Invoca-platform calls within a broader dataset of more than 70 million calls and 600 million minutes across 10 industries. These are platform-customer benchmarks, not population-representative national estimates or evidence of purchase intent.
opportunities.why_now: Newly added, recent benchmark with explicit denominator and methodology. It supports a missed-call problem_report while correcting for short misdials and quick hangups; it does not establish willingness to pay or recoverable revenue.
opportunities.value: No cash, credits, or direct savings. Problem evidence only: 52% human answer rate across Invoca's home-services platform dataset, with higher rates after excluding short calls.
opportunities.eligibility: Home-services businesses represented in Invoca's customer dataset across nine sub-industries; no public access to underlying call records and no claim that the sample represents all U.S. contractors.
opportunities.friction: Vendor-owned customer dataset and averages; sample composition may differ from small independent contractors. Does not prove a particular contractor misses calls, that a missed call was a qualified lead, or that a text-back service will recover revenue.
opportunities.observed_delta: First time this 2026 benchmark is captured in the public journal; the 52% figure is all inbound calls, while 65% and 73% exclude shorter calls.
opportunities.anti_leverage: Do not quote the benchmark as a national contractor average or convert it into guaranteed lost revenue. Use it to frame a problem hypothesis, then require customer-specific call-log evidence.

opportunities.claim: Cloudflare's November 2, 2026 first-party changelog postpones AI Search usage billing from November 1 to December 1, 2026. It states AI Search usage will not be charged before December 1 and published rates/included allowances remain unchanged. Default instance sync interval changes from 6 hours to 24 hours; supported custom intervals range from 15 minutes to 24 hours.
opportunities.eligibility: Cloudflare AI Search users on Workers Free or Paid plans. Account-specific instances, limits and billing settings are unverified.
opportunities.friction: Review any instance's configured sync interval if relying on sub-24-hour updates. More frequent syncs may consume usage allowances and later incur charges; other model/generation services can bill separately. No activation or migration is needed for this research project.
opportunities.title: Cloudflare postpones AI Search billing to December 1 and slows default sync
opportunities.value: One additional month before AI Search usage charges begin (December 1); no cash or guaranteed savings, and no waiver of separately billed Cloudflare or third-party services. Reduced default sync frequency can lower freshness for time-sensitive alerts.
opportunities.why_now: Directly contradicts the previously recorded November 1 billing-start date for this same subject, and materially changes default source freshness. The earlier entry remains immutable as historical evidence; this is a verified terms change, not a source-hash change. No active founder AI Search instance or billing exposure is established.

opportunities.claim: Official hackathon listing says student participants only, team size 2–4 required, companies/professional organizations excluded, $300 total cash prize and submission deadline November 1, 2026 at 3:00 PM Eastern.
opportunities.eligibility: Students above age of majority in allowed jurisdictions, teams of 2–4; no solo entry. Founder student status unverified, but the solo-only operating constraint is incompatible.
opportunities.friction: Must form a student team, register with organizer, build and submit within event window; less than one day remains, small prize relative to effort.
opportunities.title: TRMI x Lovhack excludes solo non-student applicants
opportunities.value: Advertised $300 cash prize for one winning team; not a grant, not available to a solo entrant.
opportunities.why_now: Time-sensitive false-positive from a broad AI-hackathon search. A public online AI event may appear open to any founder, but explicit student-only and 2–4 person team restrictions make it unsuitable for a solo independent founder without a qualifying team.

opportunities.claim: Google's official Devpost event page shows registration open for a Firebase AI Logic hybrid inference hackathon. Solo or team entries are permitted; the event lists a $10,000 cash grand prize, submissions November 9–30, 2026, closing November 30 at 2:00 PM PT. Full challenge rules, submission requirements, judging criteria and prize details are scheduled for November 9.
opportunities.eligibility: Event overview says entrants must be above age of majority and reside in an allowed country; solo participation permitted. Complete rules due November 9; individual eligibility not confirmed.
opportunities.friction: Requires qualifying hybrid on-device/cloud AI project, competition and substantial development; detailed rules not available until November 9. No entry fee is stated on overview; verify final rules.
opportunities.title: Google #BuildHybridAI 2026 accepts solo entrants; full rules pending
opportunities.value: Advertised $10,000 cash grand prize to one winner, conditional on eligibility and judging; no guaranteed credits, income, or payment.
opportunities.why_now: Newly surfaced currently open registration for solo developers; critical full eligibility and technical rules have not yet been published, so opportunity is only WATCH. Prize competition is not a paying customer or a reliable near-term income path.

opportunities.claim: Cloudflare announced October 30 that beginning November 4, 2026, D1 queries returning more than 50 MB will fail. REST API import and export operations are exempt. Cloudflare says the limit covers the 99.999th percentile of D1 queries.
opportunities.eligibility: Existing or future Cloudflare D1 users whose SQL queries return more than 50 MB; no proof that this founder currently uses D1.
opportunities.friction: Requires identifying oversized result sets, selecting needed columns and paginating. No new account, fee, or migration requirement announced.
opportunities.title: Cloudflare D1 50 MB query result ceiling effective November 4
opportunities.value: Avoid oversized-query failures; no direct cash, credits, or revenue. Pagination and narrow column selection may prevent errors.
opportunities.why_now: Newly announced dated operational constraint. Relevant to developers producing large data feeds or analytics exports; LEVERAGE//SEEKER has no verified active D1 deployment, so no immediate owner task.

opportunities.claim: As of October 30 Browser Run defaults to Chrome 152. Quick Actions default User-Agent changed from Chrome 119 to Chrome 152, /links returns absolute URLs, links-only crawls follow relative links, and Markdown output retains code block languages.
opportunities.eligibility: Browser Run is offered on Cloudflare Workers Free and Paid. Published Free allowance: 10 browser minutes/day; plan and account access unverified.
opportunities.friction: Free quota is limited; paid usage and concurrent browser fees apply beyond included Paid plan allowances. Browser scraping must respect site policies and copyright. Pricing: https://developers.cloudflare.com/browser-run/pricing/
opportunities.title: Cloudflare Browser Run Chrome 152 and improved source extraction
opportunities.value: Potentially fewer failed page reads and more reliable link normalization; not quantified and not customer revenue.
opportunities.why_now: New release improves link provenance and extraction quality for source-verified research, but any automation matching the old User-Agent may require review. No evidence the current LEVERAGE//SEEKER repository uses Browser Run.

opportunities.claim: GitHub announced GA on 2026-10-28 for Free, Team and Enterprise plans. The gh actions-lock extension can lock workflow actions, transitive dependencies and reusable workflows to exact commits; Dependabot can refresh lockfiles.
opportunities.eligibility: GitHub Actions repositories on Free, Team or Enterprise; CLI extension setup and per-workflow onboarding required.
opportunities.friction: Install and review gh actions-lock; commit generated lockfile; review dependencies for trustworthiness. No first-customer impact.
opportunities.title: GitHub Actions workflow dependency lockfiles generally available
opportunities.value: No separate license requirement announced for GitHub Free; potential avoided supply-chain incidents, not measurable revenue.
opportunities.why_now: Newly available stable dependency pinning is relevant to the public evidence repository, whose CI references version tags. This reduces unplanned dependency drift, not the need to review code.

opportunities.claim: Applications are open through 2026-11-20 for an early-stage cybersecurity incubator. The 12-week cohort has 10 company places, covers India/GCC/US, and offers up to $5,000 in KeyVigil model-gateway credits, mentorship and partner access.
opportunities.eligibility: Pre-seed/seed cybersecurity founders; idea-stage accepted with strong team and clearly defined security problem. U.S. among stated markets; individual fit and admission not established.
opportunities.friction: 12-week commitment, only 10 companies, selection process; no public application fee stated; requires cybersecurity product fit.
opportunities.title: CloudSEK Launchpad cybersecurity incubator cohort 1
opportunities.value: Up to $5,000 in KeyVigil credits for selected cohort companies; not cash, not guaranteed, not a general-purpose cloud grant.
opportunities.why_now: Newly surfaced active deadline and attractive advertised credit amount; rejected for the present LEVERAGE//SEEKER/SECONDS MATTER scope because the program explicitly targets cybersecurity founders, not general opportunity intelligence or home-service automation.
